topic: Polarity of Bonds and Dipole Moment
title: Polarity and Dipole Moment Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
In a tug of war, the stronger team pulls the rope its way. A magnet has two ends. Oil and water will not mix. Diya reads that water has a plus end and a minus end, but carbon dioxide has none. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we learn how to add up the pulls in any molecule.

On the molecule bench, the shared pair of H2 sits in the middle, then slides towards fluorine in HF: delta plus, delta minus and a crossed dipole arrow. We build the dipole moment (charge times distance, in debye, 1 D = 3.33564 x 10^-30 C m), watch the two pulls of CO2 cancel, and see why water (1.85 D) is polar. BeF2 and BF3 cancel, while the lone pair makes NH3 (4.90 x 10^-30 C m) far more polar than NF3 (0.80 x 10^-30 C m). Then polarisation and Fajans' rules with LiCl vs NaCl, an exam trap, an original exam pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 45 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
